situation.summary: Tenant Elowen Vey reports an unverified heating contractor, Bram Alder (Hearthline Boiler Service), wants to visit to check intermittent boiler pressure loss and asks for a key to be left in the shared outdoor meter cabinet. No visit is confirmed. There is no work order, the landlord has authorised only a diagnostic visit by a suitably identified contractor and has not agreed any key arrangement or entry while the tenant is out, and the contractor has not given verifiable business details. At 13:48 on 14 May the contractor texted the tenant offering Saturday 17 May 08:00-13:00 and asking for a key drop; she has not replied. The agency has sent her no message in the record, so her questions from 12 May are unanswered.
situation.task: Stop an unverified visit and a meter-cabinet key drop from going ahead, and tell the tenant where things stand.
situation.stageLabel: Visit unconfirmed; contractor identity and landlord access decision outstanding
situation.whoseMove: Us (Northbridge Lettings). The tenant is waiting on us, and the contractor's key request is open to her. Next action: tenant.update to Elowen Vey via the portal, with a one-line SMS pointing to it, now. Message: "Hello Elowen, thank you for your messages, and sorry we have not replied before now. As of today, 14 May: (1) We have not confirmed any heating visit or appointment, and neither we nor your landlord have agreed Saturday 17 May. (2) We have not agreed any key arrangement. Please do not leave a key in the meter cabinet, and do not confirm a time to the caller yet. You do not need to be at home for a visit we have not confirmed with you. (3) We are checking the caller's identity and business details with him and with your landlord. We will not share your contact details with him without your agreement. (4) Your son does not need to be asked to let anyone in. (5) If you notice a gas smell, a leak, or the heating or hot water stop, leave the property if needed, call the gas emergency number and tell us straight away. Please reply to tell us if you have had any other contact from this caller. We will update you by 12:00 on Thursday 15 May, whether or not a visit has been confirmed." Also send contractor.update to Bram Alder by email, as a second step in the same turn: "Dear Bram, your landlord has authorised a diagnostic visit at 62 Brindlewick Row for intermittent boiler pressure loss, but only by a suitably identified heating engineer. No visit is confirmed. No key arrangement or entry while the tenant is out has been agreed, so please do not ask the tenant to leave a key in the meter cabinet. Please send by 12:00 on Thursday 15 May: your company's registered name and business address, a business landline, the name of the engineer who would attend, and your public liability insurance details. We will confirm any visit in writing after we have checked these with the landlord. All access arrangements go through us, not directly with the tenant." Add to the landlord's open question (E019) that the contractor texted the tenant at 13:48 asking for a key drop; do not chase the landlord yet, since his reply is only about four hours old. Escalate to a person if the contractor cannot verify his details by Thursday 15 May, if the tenant reports a visit attempt or a key request, or if she reports any gas or CO sign.

risks.description: An unverified caller asks the tenant to leave a property key in a shared, outdoor meter cabinet. He has her mobile number from an unrecorded source, has given no business identity, and the landlord has not agreed any key arrangement. This could be a social-engineering or unauthorised-entry attempt. Do not conclude that it is fraud; stop the key drop and verify.

The contractor asked the agency for the tenant's mobile number (E016). Disclosure consent is empty (E017). The number must not be passed on without her consent, and the tenant should know that the caller already has it.
Any visit that goes ahead without the landlord's agreement to entry while the tenant is absent, or to a key arrangement, would exceed what he has authorised (E014).
Intermittent boiler pressure loss, the heating currently working (E015). No gas smell or CO sign is reported. If any appears, escalate at once.
A 15-year-old is in the household and may be home alone. The tenant does not want him asked to let anyone in. Keep this instruction in every message to the tenant and to the contractor.
The tenant has had no agency reply to her questions since 12 May (E010, E015, E018). Her 12 May questions are still open.

decision.channel: Portal, plus a short SMS pointing her to it
decision.message:
Hello Elowen,

Thank you for your messages, and I am sorry you have not had a reply from us before now.

As of today, 14 May:
1. No heating visit has been confirmed. We have not booked Saturday 17 May, and neither has your landlord. There is no work order for the property.
2. No key arrangement has been agreed. Please do not leave a key in the meter cabinet or anywhere outside the property. Please do not confirm a time with the caller for now.
3. We are checking the caller's company and identity details, and we are checking with your landlord. We will not give your contact details to anyone without your agreement.
4. Nobody will be asked to let a visitor in through your son, and he does not need to answer the door to anyone about this.
5. You told us on 13 May that you could be home on Saturday 17 May between 10:00 and 12:00. We will only offer that time to a contractor once we have checked who they are, and we will confirm the visitor's name and the reason for the visit to you in writing first. If we cannot do that in time, the visit will not go ahead on Saturday.

Please let us know if you get any more calls or messages from this number, or if anyone comes to the property about the boiler without our written confirmation. If you notice a smell of gas, call the gas emergency number straight away and then let us know. Please also tell us if the heating or hot water stops working.

We will update you by 12:00 on Thursday 15 May, whether or not a visit has been confirmed.

Kind regards,
Tamsin Rook
Northbridge Lettings

[SMS: Hi Elowen, this is Tamsin at Northbridge Lettings. No boiler visit or key arrangement has been confirmed. Please do not leave a key in the meter cabinet. I have sent you the details on the portal.]
decision.rationale: The tenant has been waiting on us since 12 May. She asked whether a visit had actually been arranged (E010), gave conditional Saturday availability (E015) and reported more contact (E018). The record shows no reply from the agency. At the decision moment the caller texted her directly to confirm Saturday 08:00–13:00 and leave the key in a shared outdoor meter cabinet (E020, E010). Nobody has authorised that: the landlord approved only a diagnostic visit by a suitably identified contractor, and agreed no entry while she is out and no external key (E014). The key-drop authorisation field and the work-order appointment are both empty (E013). The most urgent step is to stop the key drop and give the tenant the facts. This is routine handling, so a person is not needed yet: we can verify the contractor and wait for the landlord's answer to E019 ourselves. In the same turn, the contractor is told what he must provide and that access goes through us. The landlord is told about the new key request so he has it when he answers E019. His reply is only about 4 hours old, so this is not a chase.
decision.expectedOutcome: The tenant does not leave a key or confirm the caller's time, and tells us about any further contact. The contractor sends verifiable business details. The landlord confirms whether he is engaging Bram Alder and what access he authorises. If those come in, a visit can be confirmed in writing for Saturday 10:00–12:00 while the tenant is at home.
boundaries: This does not confirm or cancel any visit with the contractor. It only tells the tenant that nothing has been confirmed.
It makes no finding that the caller is or is not a genuine contractor.
It does not authorise any key arrangement or entry while the tenant is out. Only the landlord can decide that.
No tenant contact details are shared. Her consent field is empty.
It does not promise that the boiler will be looked at on Saturday.
remainingWork: Get the landlord's reply to E019: whether he is engaging Bram Alder or Hearthline, and what access he authorises.
Receive Bram Alder's business details and check them with the landlord.
If he is verified and the landlord agrees, raise a work order and confirm Saturday 17 May 10:00–12:00 in writing to the tenant and the contractor, with the tenant at home and no key drop.
Update the tenant by 12:00 on Thursday 15 May.
Escalate to a person if the details cannot be verified by Thursday, if anyone attempts a visit or asks for a key again, or if a gas or CO sign is reported.

final.rationale: The tenant has been waiting on us since 12 May. She asked whether a visit had actually been arranged (E010), gave conditional Saturday availability (E015) and reported more contact (E018). The record shows no reply from the agency. At the decision moment the caller texted her directly to confirm Saturday 08:00–13:00 and leave the key in a shared outdoor meter cabinet (E020, E010). Nobody has authorised that: the landlord approved only a diagnostic visit by a suitably identified contractor, and agreed no entry while she is out and no external key (E014). The key-drop authorisation field and the work-order appointment are both empty (E013). The most urgent step is to stop the key drop and give the tenant the facts. This is routine handling, so a person is not needed yet: we can verify the contractor and wait for the landlord's answer to E019 ourselves. In the same turn, the contractor is told what he must provide and that access goes through us. The landlord is told about the new key request so he has it when he answers E019. His reply is only about 4 hours old, so this is not a chase.
final.expectedOutcome: The tenant does not leave a key or confirm the caller's time, and tells us about any further contact. The contractor sends verifiable business details. The landlord confirms whether he is engaging Bram Alder and what access he authorises. If those come in, a visit can be confirmed in writing for Saturday 10:00–12:00 while the tenant is at home.
boundaries: This does not confirm or cancel any visit with the contractor. It only tells the tenant that nothing has been confirmed.
It makes no finding that the caller is or is not a genuine contractor.
It does not authorise any key arrangement or entry while the tenant is out. Only the landlord can decide that.
No tenant contact details are shared. Her consent field is empty.
It does not promise that the boiler will be looked at on Saturday.
remainingWork: Get the landlord's reply to E019: whether he is engaging Bram Alder or Hearthline, and what access he authorises.
Receive Bram Alder's business details and check them with the landlord.
If he is verified and the landlord agrees, raise a work order and confirm Saturday 17 May 10:00–12:00 in writing to the tenant and the contractor, with the tenant at home and no key drop.
Update the tenant by 12:00 on Thursday 15 May.
Escalate to a person if the details cannot be verified by Thursday, if anyone attempts a visit or asks for a key again, or if a gas or CO sign is reported.
assumptions: The portal and SMS are working channels to the tenant, since she has used both (E001, E003, E018).
The Wednesday 14 May morning slot has passed with no attendance recorded (E012 says it was never booked). The computed fact saying Wednesday has not been reached ignores the time of day.
Email is the working channel to the contractor and the landlord (E004, E008, E016, E019).

alternatives.whyNot: The playbook already covers this: verify the contractor, stop an unauthorised key arrangement, and refuse to share the tenant's details. No decision needs a person's authority yet. Escalation is kept for failed verification, a visit attempt, or a safety sign.
Telling the contractor matters, but the tenant is the person exposed to the key request right now and has had no reply in 2 days. The contractor message goes in alsoSend.
E019 was sent only about 4 hours ago, so a chase would be premature. The landlord gets an update with the new fact instead.
There is a live, unauthorised key request to the tenant and she has had no reply from us since 12 May.
